# Finale slide: what VERIQ does (generated from CLAIMS.md by scripts/make_slide.py; do not edit by hand)

Say every line exactly as written. Each one runs today; the proof command is in CLAIMS.md.

| # | What VERIQ does | Data / status |
|---|---|---|
| C-1 | Asks for consent before any upload, and checks file type, size, magic bytes and ZIP safety | runs |
| C-2 | Lists every place the user was asked to pay as a separate payee | runs |
| C-3 | The payee name the user saw in their own bank/UPI app is labelled "user-reported" (class A) | runs |
| C-4 | "I have already sent money" changes only the next step (to 1930), never the result | runs |
| C-5 | 1930 filing sheet keeps full identifiers; shareable summary shows accounts as last 4 digits | runs |
| C-6 | Chat text is escaped in the app and reports (no script runs, links are defanged) | runs |
| C-7 | "No major issue" always says "This is not a guarantee." | runs |
| C-8 | Cross-victim registry stores only keyed hashes: pseudonymisation, not anonymity | runs |
| C-9 | A payee links only after 2 independent reporters or a reviewer; one reporter or a burst of new reporters cannot link it | runs |
| C-10 | Payment-gateway handles are never stored or linked; a broken registry says "unavailable", never "clean" | runs |
| C-11 | Every payee gets its own answer from fixed rules (first rule that applies wins), computed live from the chat | runs |
| C-12 | An uploaded voice note goes through ffmpeg, a quality gate and AASIST, and returns flagged / no_signal / can't assess; it never crashes and never clears a payee | runs (calibrated with our trained head, see C-23; B's ASVspoof calibration not run yet) |
| C-13 | More risk never gives a milder answer; a voice result never clears a payee; "unavailable" is never "clean" | runs |
| C-14 | Gateway names, personal-looking names, initials and near spellings are "unverified", never an accusation | runs |
| C-15 | A judge can change the typed payee name and the answer is recomputed on the spot | runs |
| C-16 | On the held-out synthetic test (generated by us), 300 chats: every payee found (399/399), 0 false alarms on 178 genuine payees, 0 scams cleared; 96.2% of answers as expected when first run blind, 100% after the Q2 fix for shop names that contain a person's name (that fix was made after seeing the failures, so 100% is not a blind number) | runs (synthetic) |
| C-17 | A UPI ID hidden in a QR screenshot is found and checked like any other payee; if the QR's own name differs from the claimed firm, the answer is "needs review" (the QR name is sender-typed, so it never decides alone) | runs |
| C-18 | A look-alike account ("NAVYUG ONLINE TRADERS" for "Navyug Broking") goes to review instead of passing as the firm; genuine variants still match | runs |
| C-19 | Obfuscated pressure phrases ("gu@r@nteed", "u_r_g_e_n_t", "P.a.y t@x to withdraw", Hinglish) are still caught | runs |
| C-20 | A short or unclear voice note plus pressure to pay an unverified payee gives "Don't pay yet: high pressure" | runs |
| C-21 | A genuine user flagged by mistake can ask for a review in one step; a reviewer overturns or upholds with a reason; the original result and an audit trail (no raw identifiers) are kept; time to decision is shown | runs |
| C-22 | 1930 / NCRP incident card (JSON): every field the complaint asks for, blanks left blank, file hashes and timeline; not an official format | runs |
| C-23 | We trained a voice classifier on AASIST embeddings during the finale; IN-DOMAIN (unseen FSDD speakers and Kokoro voices) it catches 69% of synthetic clips (pretrained: 15%), AUC 0.82 vs 0.669 and flags 19% of genuine clips. Cross-dataset it fails (C-30), so it is off by default | runs (synthetic/public data) |
| C-24 | A judge can paste any chat text and get a computed answer | runs |
| C-25 | The app shows its own measured results and failure cases (How accurate is VERIQ?) | runs |
| C-26 | One command (`make reproduce` / `reproduce.ps1`) regenerates our synthetic data byte for byte from seeded generators, re-runs every test and benchmark, and compares each number with the committed one | runs |
| C-27 | Test completeness is measured: about 93% of product code statements run under the tests (pinned environment), 17 deliberately planted safety bugs are each caught by the tests, and the suite passes in two random orders | runs |
| C-28 | Hostile and broken inputs (empty, oversized, zip bombs, wrong encodings, no timestamps, mixed Hindi/English, 0-second or corrupt audio, locked registry) give a clear refusal or "can't assess", never a crash or a reassuring answer | runs |
| C-29 | On ASVspoof 2019 LA eval clips (100 real + 100 synthetic, each also mp3 and Opus), pretrained AASIST scores AUC 0.77 / EER 0.32 and, at a threshold fitted on LA dev, flags 16% of genuine clips and misses 56% of synthetic ones. IN-DISTRIBUTION: AASIST was trained on this dataset | runs (public data, user-reported laptop run) |
| C-30 | Our trained voice head does NOT transfer: on the same ASVspoof eval clips it scores AUC 0.46 (chance) and flags 54% of genuine clips, so it is off by default and voice stays a review cue | runs (public data) |
| C-31 | "Delete my data" removes everything VERIQ holds in the session and its temporary folders, shown before and after; a voice note leaves no file behind; the registry file contains no raw UPI ID or account number | runs |
| C-32 | A judge can run VERIQ on an unknown test kit (voice notes, videos' audio, QR images, chats; labels from a CSV or folder names) and get per-file answers plus a report with accuracy, precision, recall, false-positive rate, abstentions and 95% intervals; one bad file never stops the run | runs |
| C-33 | A scenario player replays scams (A, B, C) and a genuine broker flagged by mistake (D) message by message; the answer is recomputed after every message and after any edit; D shows the review and the time to decision | runs |
| C-34 | Name matcher on 97 labelled name pairs (written by us, after the matcher): 0/42 same-firm names wrongly called a mismatch (3/42 before the 25 Oct fixes), 36/36 unrelated businesses caught, 0 non-firm names called a match | runs (specification check, not blind) |
| C-37 | A voice head trained on two sources (FSDD/Kokoro + ASVspoof LA dev), threshold by grouped cross-validation, flags 5.1% of genuine and catches 44% of synthetic clips on held-out LA eval (and 7.5% / 40% on held-out FSDD/Kokoro); heads trained on one source fail on the other (AUC 0.58 / 0.63). Not installed: no third-dataset test | runs (public + synthetic data) |
| C-38 | Installs and runs with no internet: offline wheel bundle, one-command install, and a smoke test (parse, engine, voice clip, registry, report, app health) that also proves VERIQ's code makes no outgoing connection | runs (Linux sandbox; Windows offline bundle not run) |
| C-39 | Voice notes are scored by pretrained AASIST with the threshold Claude B fitted on ASVspoof 2019 LA dev, as a WEAK review cue only: a flag sends the payee to human review; "no signal" never clears or softens an answer. On LA eval (close to the model's training data) that threshold flags 16% of genuine clips, misses 56% of synthetic ones and abstains on 9.5%; In-the-Wild not run; our synthetic demo clip is missed | runs (public data) |
| C-40 | The alert says why it fired and offers four actions (do not pay, check the name in your bank app, ask a person to review, download a report pack); safeguards are tested as running: no chat or audio left on disk after a full check, offline mode blocks every outgoing connection, delete-my-data clears the session | runs |
| C-41 | A genuine user flagged by mistake (scenario D) is cleared with 1 user click and 1 reviewer click after the alert; the app's own processing time is about half a second (human checking time not included); the audit trail keeps no raw payee identifier | runs (synthetic scenario) |
| C-42 | Live journey on 5 varied inputs written for the run (English, Hinglish, Devanagari, changed payee wording and amounts): 5 as expected after the 25 Oct extractor fix (before it, 1 miss: a UPI ID broken up with spaces) | runs (inputs written by us, not tuned on) |
| C-43 | Pre-registered run on an AI-generated blind chat set (n=80, author model not recorded), code as committed: 28/40 scam chats warned, 1/40 called "no major issue", 7/40 genuine chats accused. After fixes made from those failures (NOT blind): 35/40 warned, 0/40 missed, 1/40 genuine accused | runs (AI-generated; 12 chats seen once before the run, results also given for the 68 unseen) |
| C-44 | Name pairs written by AI with sight of the engine (NOT blind, n=200): another entity's name called a "match" 4/100 before, 1/100 after the fixes; same firm called a discrepancy 2/70 before, 0/70 after | runs (not blind, optimistic) |
| C-45 | Payee extraction on AI-written lines (NOT blind, n=100): UPI and account recall 18/53 before, 50/53 after the fixes (obfuscated UPI IDs, grouped digits); precision 50/52 | runs (not blind, optimistic) |
| C-46 | A chat that asks for payment only through a link gets "check before you pay: VERIQ can't see who receives a link payment" instead of "nothing found" | runs |

**Not run yet (say so if asked):** C-35 Pressure cues on the public UCI SMS Spam Collection (not UPI fraud): false-alarm rate on normal messages; C-36 Blind chats written by teammates who did not read the rules: scams warned, scams cleared, false alarms on genuine chats

Data: chats are synthetic (generated by us) or written blind by teammates; voice data is public (ASVspoof 2019 LA, FSDD) or synthetic (Kokoro TTS). No real victims' data. Claude (Anthropic) was used to write code and documents. No partnership with I4C, SEBI, RBI, NPCI or any bank is claimed. VERIQ can be fooled: see the evasion lab.
